newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX vaults 4,100 points on dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX vaults 4,100 points on dlr gains.

text.p: German shares shot to fresh highs in pre-bourse trade on Monday as export shares received a firm boost from the strong dollar and dealers said the outlook for the market was positive.
"What we've seen so far is perfectly justified with the dollar at this level," said a Frankfurt trader.
"Export shares look set to be the outperformers today. It just remains to be seen how the follow-up orders come through."
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was up 32.68 points at 4,106.98 points at 0720 GMT. The index hit resistance at 4,110 points, dealers said, and there was a chance the rally would slow.
The September DTB DAX futures contract was up 44 points at 4,136.0 points.
The dollar's continued strong performance against the mark, against which it is trading at a six-year high, was the focus of all attention.

Dollar-sensitive chemical, engineering and car shares were leading the early advance. Drugs group Schering AG was up 4.10 marks, or two percent, at 200 marks while BASF AG was up 1.14 marks, or 1.7 percent, at 68.50 marks.
Siemens AG, continuing a run of popularity, was up 1.85 marks at 115.80 marks.
